bull_bear.body: Prioritizing completion of Dahej rebuild and Pakhajan greenfield; Promoter infusion of INR 161cr via preferential allotment; Final dividend INR 1/share; No major standalone capex planned post-FY27 until stabilization.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commissioning delays (Dahej labor shortage already caused slight slip); Lithium/Bromine price volatility (though mostly pass-through); Customer qualification timelines for giga-factories; Execution risk on INR 1,800cr+ project scale-up; Geopolitical supply chain disruptions.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident on strategic pivot and technology differentiation (Morita partnership); Pragmatic on timeline revisions (design optimization); Transparent on cost increases but firm on ROCE targets; Optimistic on non-FEOC demand visibility.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Capex revision driven by 'design-led optimization' and Japanese tech integration actually aims to lower long-term opex/import dependence rather than just scope creep; Actuarial assumption change artificially boosted Q4 profits by reducing employee costs; Inventory build-up was strategic pre-stocking for Q1/Q2 FY27 due to Dahej delay, not demand slowdown.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The Board has approved raising up to INR 600 crore via a Qualified Institutional Placement (in INR or foreign currency), subject to shareholder and statutory approvals.
- The capex cycle is debt-funded for now: consolidated net debt jumped from INR 530 crore in FY25 to INR 1,295 crore in FY26 against net worth of INR 816 crore, and finance costs rose 64% YoY.
- Long track record of equity-led funding for growth — INR 132 crore IPO (2019), ~INR 225 crore preferential allotment (2021), ~INR 253 crore preferential (2023), INR 200 crore NCDs (2024) and INR 161 crore promoter preferential infusion (2026).
- Dahej fire insurance is a meaningful cash source: cumulative recoveries of INR 164 crore to date (INR 155 crore on-account claims including an INR 15 crore July 2026 tranche, plus INR 9 crore salvage), with a net claim receivable of INR 186 crore on a consolidated basis; delayed insurance receipts are inflating working capital.
- No dividend policy is discussed; all capital is directed at the battery-materials build-out and core capacity restoration.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

business.body: Organic Chemicals: INR 194cr (+7% YoY, ~45% Bromine, ~30% Intermediates, balance Li); Inorganic Chemicals: INR 53cr (+145% YoY, volume-driven stockpiling ahead of price hikes); Neogen Ionics: INR 13cr (Q4), INR 36cr (FY26), mostly salts.
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for non-FEOC compliant, reliable battery material supply chain for US/Global OEMs | Neogen Chemicals Ltd | beneficiary | High | Only Indian player with Morita tech partnership for LiPF6; audits completed for US makers; positioned as primary alternative to China. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- Leading manufacturer of Bromine- and Lithium-based specialty chemicals operating since 1991 (incorporated 1989), with 258 products developed by in-house R&D, 4 manufacturing sites and 2 R&D facilities.
- Describes itself as the largest importer of Lithium Carbonate in India for the last three decades, giving it direct relationships with global lithium miners and processors — a stated entry barrier alongside its specialised business model.
- Neogen Ionics is positioned as a preferred non-FEOC partner for domestic and global cell makers: provisional approvals from 4 major international customers and completed final site audits for 3 US-based electrolyte manufacturers.
- Diversified end-markets span pharmaceuticals, agrochemicals, flavours & fragrances, semiconductors/electronic chemicals, specialty polymers, vapour-absorption chillers and battery chemicals; exports were 30% of Q1 FY27 revenue across the USA, Europe, Middle East, China, Korea and Japan.
- Promoters are technocrats with over six decades of cumulative domain experience; founder Dr. Haridas Kanani built India's first indigenous-technology Bromine plant and grew Neogen 750x over 35 years.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Policy] India's PLI scheme for ACC batteries carries an INR 18,100 crore outlay for 50 GWh of capacity and mandates 60% domestic value addition within 5 years, with a further 10 GWh re-bidding tranche (INR 3,620 crore outlay) and a proposed PLI for battery components that would push cell makers to localise raw-material sourcing.
- [Regulation] To claim the US 45X tax credit, US Li-ion cell producers must meet Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) rules, forcing a shift to non-FEOC suppliers with full transition expected by 2027 — the core demand driver behind Neogen Ionics' international engagement.
- [Industry] India battery demand is projected at 33 GWh (2025), 92 GWh (2027) and 236 GWh (2032), while by 2030 non-China demand is estimated at 1,125 KT of electrolyte and 141 KT of lithium salts.
- [Corporate structure] Buli Chemicals India (Patancheru) was merged into Neogen in January 2025; Neogen Morita New Materials Limited was incorporated as a 100% subsidiary of Neogen Ionics, and a JV was executed between Neogen Ionics and Morita Investment.
- [Seasonality] The business is structurally H2-weighted: European demand scales from October-November and accelerates after January, lithium-chemical demand peaks in Q4 on HVAC capex enjoying 100% depreciation benefits, and agrochemical demand follows the H2 crop cycle — management urges only like-for-like YoY quarterly comparisons.
business.title: Notable from the deck

latest_quarter.body: EBITDA margin 17.8% pressured by expansion overheads, geopolitical input costs, and Dahej transition costs; Strategic pass-through mechanisms protected core profitability; Battery projects targeted at 18-20% ROCE despite INR 250cr+ capex revision due to tech optimization.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Standalone Revenue FY27: INR 875-950cr (ex-battery); Battery Revenue FY27: >INR 300cr (skewed H2); Margins: Targeting 18-20% ROCE on battery projects; Order Inflow: Commercial supplies expected Jul-Aug 2026 for salts; Capex: INR 600-700cr remaining in FY27.
outlook.title: Guidance

outlook.body: Transitioning from pilot/qualification to commercial; 3 US electrolyte makers completed audits; 1 domestic giga-customer qualified & buying; 1 domestic mega-customer qualified for pilot; 2 additional giga-customers testing vs China; 2 more in discussion for 2027 start.
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: FY28 battery revenue potential INR 1,200-1,400cr; FY29 total revenue potential INR 2,400-2,900cr; Capacity expansion beyond current 8kT salt/30kT electrolyte dependent on demand; Semiconductor approvals for organolithium pending.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

deepdive.thesis: Neogen delivered resilient Q4FY26 core growth (22% YoY revenue) driven by volumes, while strategically pivoting capital towards battery materials with revised capex ensuring 18-20% ROCE. The imminent commissioning of Dahej (Jun-26) and Pakhajan (H1/H2 FY27) plants marks a fundamental inflection point, transitioning the company from a specialty chemical player to a integrated battery materials manufacturer with significant revenue optionality in FY27/FY28.

open.item: CSM currently at 15-18% of revenue; target to reach 20% by next year (FY26).
Target to reach 20% of revenue from CSM business (currently maintaining upward of 15%); hope to cross 20% by next financial year, or this year if agro recovers in H2.
By FY26 target non-battery revenue mix of 40% Bromine Derivatives, 20% CSM, 20% Advanced Intermediates (CSM+AI together 40%), 20% non-battery lithium/inorganic salts.
Dahej replacement facility construction progressing rapidly; commissioning on track for June 2026.
Dahej SEZ organic plant rebuild on track to be operational in Q1 FY27; will get one-year moratorium once online.
Pakhajan greenfield: commercial electrolyte manufacturing targeted H1 FY27, electrolyte salts H2 FY27; mechanical assembly complete, in trial run phase.
Morita's planned equity contribution of $20 million towards the JV expected during H1 FY27; building India's first non-FEOC compliant electrolyte salt platform.
Three US electrolyte makers completed audits (corrections to be closed in 1-2 months); commercial electrolyte supply from Dahej expected to start by July or August 2026 without further approvals.

Added 500 MT intermediate lithium-compound capacity at Dahej (over and above 5,500 MT salt+additive) as starting material, in discussion to sell to Morita (China) and other LiPF6 producers for China-free supply.

Organolithium capacity increased 2.5x (120 to 300 MT/year); reached highest-ever monthly volume in March 2026, targeting 80-90% of increased capacity this year with possible small further capacity CAPEX.
Dahej Phase 1 project budgeted at INR 428 crore, on track for completion by February 2027 (remaining 1,000 tons + 500 tons intermediate by Q3, some capacity Q4).
Pakhajan Phase 2 revised cost INR 1,367 crore, expected completion by March 2027 (SCOD approved by lenders).

Confident of standalone (non-battery) revenue of INR 875-950 crore in FY27 (vs original INR 950-1,000 cr, trimmed for Dahej start delay); trying to hit INR 950 cr+ via organolithium/lithium outperformance.
Battery (Neogen Ionics) revenue guidance of more than INR 300 crore in FY27, majority in H2 with sequential quarterly improvement.
Cumulative on-account insurance claims received INR 140 crore plus INR 7 crore salvage; net claim receivable INR 203 crore, working with insurers to expedite final settlement.
By end FY27, gross block expected ~INR 1,700-1,800 crore for Neogen Ionics and INR 450-550 crore standalone (~INR 40-50 cr above pre-fire on rebuild).
Replacement plant for fire-hit Dahej at adjacent location; civil foundation done, long-lead equipment ordered; on track to be operational by next year (FY27).

No significant organic/inorganic CAPEX in FY25 and FY26 (existing capacity supports ~Rs. 1,000 crore standalone); consider debottlenecking in FY27 for ~15% growth and organic CAPEX likely FY27 for FY28-29 growth.
Initiated early-stage contract manufacturing with 4-5 companies including 2-3 new agrochem projects (one using bromine + n-Butyl lithium) and 2 pharma projects; meaningful contribution beyond FY26.
Enabling resolution to infuse up to Rs. 500 crore into Neogen Ionics via CCDs (quasi-equity) gradually over 3 years; ~Rs. 220 crore already invested to be converted.

verdicts.note: Pakhajan commercial production now H1 FY27 (mechanical assembly done, trial run), not FY26.

verdicts.item: Battery chemicals FY26 revenue expected in the range of Rs. 300-500 crore (upper end Rs. 500 cr per capacity), depending on approval timing and electrolyte demand ramp; more precise number by May call.
